description: PRD US-01 AC1 (the manager is notified of a new request) and US-03 (the employee is notified of the decision) have no implementation today: the biggest gap against the original requirements. A bell in the top bar shows each person's unread notifications. Events: a request is submitted (its manager), a request is approved, rejected or overridden (the employee), a request is overridden (also its manager). Email notifications are an OPTIONAL last slice (TASK-056, only if time). Risk to respect: the top bar runs on every page, so the count must be ONE cheap indexed statement inside the page query budget (POOL_MAX - 1), streamed so it never blocks a page.

One migration, types.ts in the same change: notifications (id, recipient_id fk users, kind (submitted, approved, rejected, overridden), leave_request_id fk, created_at, read_at nullable). No free text from users (the message is built from kind and the request at read time, so no personal data is copied). RLS deny-by-default, index (recipient_id, created_at desc) and a partial index on unread, no hard delete (trigger like the other tables); read_at may be updated once. Verify probes and a gated real-database test with mutations.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a notification can be inserted for a recipient and read_at can be set but the row cannot be deleted or truncated;AC2: the unread read for one recipient uses the index and never returns another person's rows;AC3: types.ts mirrors the migration and the schema verification passes;AC4: the seed runs twice with no change

summary: Write notifications in the existing transactions
description: In the SAME transaction as each event: createLeaveRequest inserts a submitted notification for the person's manager (US-01 AC1); decideLeaveRequest inserts approved or rejected for the employee (US-03); the HR override route inserts overridden for the employee and the manager. A failure to notify rolls the whole event back (the audit row is already in the same transaction), so nothing is half-done. No notification to the actor. Update the existing tests and add one per event, with exact recipients (Leo's request never notifies Marco).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: submitting a request notifies the employee's manager and nobody else;AC2: approving or rejecting notifies the employee;AC3: an override notifies the employee and their manager;AC4: the event and its notification commit or roll back together;AC5: no notification goes to the person who acted

description: GET /api/notifications (the session user's latest 20 with the request's employee, type and dates read in one statement, plus the unread count) and POST /api/notifications/read (marks the session user's notifications read, optionally one id), both wrapped in withErrorHandling, zod validated, scoped by recipient_id = the session user in the SQL, never a client user id. Marking read is a write, so it is a route handler (rule 11), not a server action. Tests: another person's notification can never be read or marked (403/empty), an unknown id is a no-op not an error leak.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the list and count contain only the session user's notifications, newest first;AC2: marking read changes only the session user's rows and a foreign id changes nothing;AC3: unauthenticated callers get 401 in the standard envelope;AC4: the count is one statement

description: A bell in the top bar for every signed-in role: an unread badge (text count, not colour alone), a dropdown list (Escape and outside click close it, focus returns to the bell) built from kind, person and dates, each row marking itself read, a Mark all as read action, an empty state and an error state that does not break the page. The unread count is read once per page in a streamed Suspense section on its own statement so the layout stays within POOL_MAX - 1 (update the query budget test for the layout). A client component only for the dropdown; mobile first, 44px targets, labelled, keyboard-usable. Rows link to Team Approvals or My Balance where the target exists.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the bell shows the unread count and the list for the signed-in person;AC2: marking one or all read updates the badge;AC3: the layout plus any page stays within the query budget and a failed read shows the bell without a count and nothing else breaks;AC4: keyboard and screen-reader usable and no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px

description: Only if time. After the transaction commits, send a short email for the same events through an SMTP sender (nodemailer with SMTP_* variables added to env.ts and .env.example with comments; never read process.env elsewhere). A send failure NEVER fails or rolls back the leave action: it is logged (no addresses or bodies) and skipped. One email per event, no personal reasons or notes in the body, a link only. Respect the provider's rate limit (Gmail demo sender or a verified-domain provider, see TASK-045). Per-user opt-out is out of scope.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an event sends one email to the same recipients as the in-app notification;AC2: a mail failure does not affect the leave action and is logged without personal data;AC3: no secret or recipient list is logged;AC4: env variables are validated and documented

description: End to end on a real engine: submit as Elena (Marco notified), approve and reject (Elena notified), override (Elena and her manager notified), and the other-team user never sees or marks anything; the query budget for every page including the layout; browser check as employee, manager and HR at 1440, 375 and 320 px; full quality gate; retro.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: each event notifies exactly the expected recipients on a real engine;AC2: no cross-person read or mark-read is possible;AC3: the quality gate passes and the query budget stays green;AC4: the browser check passes at 1440, 375 and 320 px for all roles
